note:
The ATTENTION register on a board card. Both sides mark the SAME card — LW-142, lane index 1, card index 0 — because the live fixture rides the one trusted signal BoardRenderer accepts (a SurfaceFieldChange whose field indexes items_path). PRD-01 requirement 5: accent border + 2px inset accent bar, and NOT the board's plum identity hue, which stays on the kicker dot. So `changed.card` borderColor/boxShadow are the two rows this state exists to check, and `card.kicker-dot` is the control that must NOT have moved.

Same two read-past caveats as anchors/board.json: the functional-mode oklch neutral ladder puts one systemic delta on every background, and the decorative kicker dot inherits its parent's type (read only its backgroundColor/boxShadow/size).

elements.label: card.kicker-dot
elements.note: Unchanged from the at-rest state on purpose: identity must not react to a pending decision.

elements.label: changed.card
elements.note: THE anchor of this state. Design: border-color --accent-line + box-shadow inset 2px 0 0 --accent. Live composes both as inline styles, which outrank any stylesheet rule, so what is measured here is what ships.

elements.label: changed.transition-chip
elements.note: The mock states the transition in words on the card — an accent chip reading "→ In review". Live now renders the same statement, so this is bound rather than design-only. It was DESIGN-ONLY until the chip existed; leaving it unbound now would keep reporting an absence that has been closed.

elements.label: changed.sr-marker
elements.note: LIVE-ONLY on purpose (no design selector). The screen-reader word behind the colour-only mark. Reports as an INFO extra; it is here so the report shows the accessibility answer exists.

elements.label: unchanged.sibling
elements.note: The control card in the same lane: the mark must not spread. If this one also reports an accent border, the mark is leaking.

unmapped.why: The mock's proposed state also renders an explanatory note above the board ("LW-142 moves In progress → In review …"). That belongs to the approval flow, not to PRD-01's card mark, and PRD-01 scopes itself to the current-state view. Excluded deliberately rather than filed as drift.
Same reason — the mock's proposed state carries an approve/reject bar. Approval chrome is host-owned (TcSurfaceMount renders the controls), not part of the board renderer PRD-01 changes.
